guard_streams.source: Ofcom communications services for disabled people

facts.detail: Disabled customers unable to use a printed directory can receive free directory enquiries with call through-connection.
Priority fault repair applies to landline and broadband, not mobile, where a disabled person has a genuine urgent need.
Priority-repair charges must not exceed the provider's standard fault-repair charge.
A disabled customer can nominate a friend or relative to help manage bills.

guard_streams.write_limit: Accessibility services are customer rights and do not prove parcel coverage or measured performance.

facts.detail: Landline and mobile companies must provide access to an approved text relay service.
Text relay is intended for people with hearing or speech impairments.
The service converts text to speech and speech to text through a relay assistant.
Ofcom approves relay providers and sets minimum service standards.

guard_streams.write_limit: Text-relay availability cannot populate fixed-broadband parcel fields.

facts.detail: Providers must maintain clear and effective policies for identifying and fairly treating vulnerable customers.
Specific disability duties include priority fault repair, text relay and free directory enquiries.
Deaf British Sign Language users can access a free video relay service for emergency organisations.
Customers needing an accessible format because of disability can request communications-service information in formats such as Braille or large print.

guard_streams.write_limit: Emergency and accessible-format rights do not establish network serviceability at an address.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom unable to pay a bill guide

facts.detail: Customers having difficulty paying should contact their provider as soon as possible.
Possible options include a cheaper package, repayment over time, affordable monthly amounts or a changed payment date.
The provider is not automatically obliged to offer every listed option.
Unpaid accounts may first be restricted, potentially leaving only emergency and provider calls while incoming calls continue.

guard_streams.write_limit: Billing and disconnection guidance cannot demonstrate parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Ofcom research found 83% of people who sought debt-support information turned to their provider.
The cited monitoring data showed just over 2% missed at least one payment and less than 1% missed two or more.
Only 53% of people experiencing telecoms debt recalled receiving provider information about debt support.
Expected support includes time to seek help, flexible repayment, tariff advice and referral to free debt support.

guard_streams.write_limit: Debt-support statistics are national customer-care evidence, not parcel availability.

facts.detail: Providers should prevent disconnection wherever possible while customers seek help.
Good practice includes payment holidays, deferrals or freezing additional fees and charges.
Providers should discuss realistic, reasonable and flexible repayment plans.
Providers should offer tariff advice, refer to free debt organisations and use multiple communication channels.

guard_streams.write_limit: Best-practice support cannot be converted into exact network data.

facts.detail: Ofcom fined Virgin Media £23.8 million for vulnerable-customer failures.
Telecare customers were disconnected during the digital-landline migration process.
Disconnection prevented affected telecare devices from reaching alarm-monitoring centres while the restriction remained.
Ofcom concluded the provider failed to follow its own vulnerability policies and breached consumer-protection rules.

guard_streams.write_limit: An enforcement finding does not establish parcel-level network performance.

facts.detail: Gigaclear holds two Project Gigabit contracts for North and South Oxfordshire.
The combined contract value is £26.5 million.
The contracts target around 10,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contracts were signed in November 2023 and require detailed planning and construction before service access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Awarded contract scope is not current parcel orderability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Buckinghamshire Hertfordshire and East Berkshire redesign

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 34,000 premises for £58 million.
The original contract was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign reduced scope to around 6,000 premises backed by £24.4 million.
The redesign followed commercial expansion, and premise lists remain subject to planning and technical change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Redesigned regional totals cannot be promoted to exact parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Bedfordshire Northamptonshire and Milton Keynes redesign

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 25,000 premises for £51 million.
The original contract was signed in February 2024.
The May 2026 redesign reduced scope to around 6,000 premises backed by £19.8 million.
Planning and physical build are required before service, and scope may change for planning or technical reasons.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract redesign and anticipated access do not prove current service at a parcel.

facts.detail: Connect Fibre is the supplier for the Derbyshire contract.
The contract value is £33 million.
The award targets more than 17,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in November 2023 and requires planning and network construction before service.

guard_streams.write_limit: A regional award cannot establish exact current parcel availability.
